clue.text: Place for cowards only? Troops couldn't take it

definitions.text: Place for cowards only? Troops couldn't take it

parts.words: Place for cowards only? Troops couldn't take it
parts.note: read jokily, a spot belonging to no brave man suits only cowards; in fact it is the deadly strip between front lines that neither army could capture

explanation.surface: A sneer at a hideout fit only for the faint-hearted, which soldiers would never deign to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: The ground between opposing trenches is held by neither side, so no army can take it, and the clue jokes that only non-men would go there.

clue.text: Book of a kind not seen before

definitions.meaning: a long work of prose fiction

definitions.text: of a kind not seen before
definitions.meaning: new and original, as an idea can be

explanation.surface: A description of a groundbreaking book.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a fictional book; the adjective means fresh and original, never encountered before.

clue.text: Fat fish inhabiting the sea all around

indicators.note: a fish living in something sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
the sea surrounds the fish on every side, confirming that it encloses the fish's letters

parts.note: marine means of the sea, and the marine can mean the sea or seafaring
a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A plump fish swimming with the ocean on every side.
explanation.walkthrough: Two container signals, 'inhabiting' and 'all around', both describe the fish sitting inside the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a spreadable fat used in place of butter.

clue.text: Owners and I deny helter-skelter provides a short-lived sensation

indicators.note: helter-skelter means in confused disorder, so the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Proprietors and the speaker refuse to admit that the fairground slide was a passing craze.
explanation.walkthrough: A helter-skelter is also a spiral fairground slide, which the surface leans on; here it signals the jumble of OWNERS AND I DENY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine days' wonder is an idiom for something that causes a stir and is quickly forgotten.

clue.text: Swimmer, svelte and sunburned, turned up

parts.note: svelte means slim, lean

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word turned up is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: sunburned skin is red

explanation.surface: A slim, tanned swimmer arriving at the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' turns RED into DER beneath LEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit Hero, so he is the archetypal swimmer.

clue.text: New member of the RAF guarding a couple of interlinked units

indicators.note: a guard stands around what it protects, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: an erk is British slang for a low-ranking aircraftman in the Royal Air Force
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A fresh RAF recruit keeps watch over two linked units.
explanation.walkthrough: An erk is RAF slang that solvers outside Britain may not know; 'guarding' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A network is a system of connected parts, such as computers or stations, linked together.

clue.text: State provided for neglected child

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for Washington State (or Western Australia)
provided that means if

explanation.surface: Asking whether the state cares for an abandoned youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A waif is a homeless, uncared-for child, a stray left to fend alone.

clue.text: Emotion displayed by fisherman who's lost line

indicators.note: losing something means it is removed from the word

parts.note: an angler fishes with rod and line

explanation.surface: The frustration of an angler whose line has snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is a strong feeling of displeasure, one of the basic human emotions.

clue.text: Stupid and macrocephalic

definitions.meaning: having an abnormally large head, read literally as big-skulled

explanation.surface: Insulting someone as both dim and big-skulled.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for dimwitted, taken literally, describes someone with an oversized head, which is what macrocephalic means.

clue.text: Social occasion in Lincolnshire giving rise to protest

parts.note: Boston is a market town in Lincolnshire, an English county
a tea party is a social gathering over tea

explanation.surface: A tea gathering in an English county that sparks a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: BOSTON is a town in Lincolnshire, on England's east coast; the famous protest happened in its Massachusetts namesake.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1773 dumping of tea into Boston harbour was a celebrated protest against British taxation.

clue.text: Stoop over and accept embraces

indicators.note: the words hold the answer within them, as arms embrace something

explanation.surface: Bend down and accept a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoop' looks like a verb; it is the American word for a porch.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoop in American English is a porch or small raised platform at a house's entrance, like a veranda.

clue.text: Considered joint time after time

indicators.note: after means the earlier pieces follow this one in the answer

parts.note: a hough is a joint of meat from the hock

explanation.surface: A joint smoked over and over, after much deliberation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint time' gives HOUGH + T, and 'after time' puts another T in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered and thought are both past tenses of verbs meaning pondered or reflected.

clue.text: Fancifully laud London, lacking nothing as a holidaydestination

indicators.note: done fancifully means rearranged in an imaginative way
lacking means one letter is missing from the jumbled pool

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Praising the capital in flights of fancy, minus anything to back it up, in a holiday brochure.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove an O from LAUDLONDON and rearrange the rest. LLANDUDNO is a seaside resort in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a Victorian seaside resort on the north Wales coast, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Brief leaders in the Sunday Express about royalty

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other piece
the leaders of words are their first letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch

explanation.surface: Short editorials in a tabloid on the royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ER inside TSE, the first letters of The Sunday Express.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse and brief both mean short and to the point.

clue.text: Friendship — where would girl be without it?

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the girl's name goes round the other word

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A wistful question about where a girl would be without companionship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations, goodwill between people or nations.

clue.text: Attack I put together on attachment

parts.note: a disease attacks or affects a part of the body

explanation.surface: An assault assembled from parts of an attachment.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection is fondness, an emotional attachment to someone.

clue.text: Revived king in control, but duke went first

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to rein in is to control
K is the chess abbreviation for king
led means went in front, went first

explanation.surface: A king brought back to power, with a duke leading the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revived' sits at the front as the definition; the comma-free 'in control' tempts a reading of LED alone, but control is the rein.
explanation.definitionFit: Rekindled means set alight again, so figuratively revived or renewed.

clue.text: Visit pub first -— it's not a long distance

indicators.note: first means this piece goes ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
to call on someone is to visit

explanation.surface: Drop in at the pub before anything else, since it is only round the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts LOCAL ahead of CALL, though the clue gives it second.
explanation.definitionFit: A local call is a telephone call within the same area, the opposite of a long-distance call.

clue.text: Available to go round coast

parts.note: free means available
to wheel is to turn or go round

explanation.surface: A free pass to tour the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast or freewheel is to move along without pedalling or power.

clue.text: Gospel upset part of church set

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
a jelly sets, or gels

explanation.surface: A Bible reading that disturbed a group of churchgoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NAVE into EVAN, then GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an archaic word for the gospel, the Christian good news.

clue.text: Look these days outside our island for medieval weapon

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look

indicators.note: outside means the word stands around the other piece

parts.note: now means these days
GB, Great Britain, is the island the British setter calls ours

explanation.surface: An invitation to see an ancient arm displayed beyond Britain's shores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our island' is the British setter's Great Britain; 'outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The longbow was the tall English bow that won battles such as Agincourt in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Hero in the Spanish police

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is a branch of the British police

explanation.surface: A heroic figure in the Spanish police force.
explanation.definitionFit: El Cid was the eleventh-century Castilian warrior, a national hero of Spain.

clue.text: Take taxi home to house

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
in means at home

explanation.surface: Catch a cab back to your house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to confine or shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cabin is to confine or shut up in a small space, as one houses something.

clue.text: Bachelor given loan by union

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for Bachelor, as in a degree
to lend is to loan

explanation.surface: A single man lent money by his trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend is a mixture, a union of different things combined.

clue.text: Opals in an arrangement that's capital

indicators.note: an arrangement sets things in a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A jeweller's display of opals that is excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like an adjective meaning excellent; it is a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Annapolis is the capital city of the US state of Maryland.

clue.text: The strength of various wines

indicators.note: various means differing in arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A remark on how strong different wines are.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means a tendon, and by extension muscular strength or power.

clue.text: Lettuce shunned by sailors?

definitions.meaning: a crisp, round variety of salad leaf
a floating mass of ice that ships steer well clear of

explanation.surface: A salad leaf that seafarers refuse to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceberg is a crisp lettuce variety, and a floating ice mass that mariners avoid.

clue.text: Negotiate terms bringing profit to pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
gain means profit

explanation.surface: Haggling over a deal that will make a pub money.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to haggle, negotiating the terms of a deal.

clue.text: Knot done wrongly

indicators.note: done wrongly means put together the wrong way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knot tied badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knot or knob, as on a plant stem or in a network.

clue.text: Sudden misfortune (a love-child) explained in great detail

parts.note: a blow is a sudden setback or shock
a by-blow is an old word for an illegitimate child

explanation.surface: The shock of an illegitimate birth, recounted at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow-by-blow account describes events in full, step by step, as a fight commentary does.
